Tap it continuously, and say this out loud with me.
How strong is the feeling now, from zero to ten? If it's still above a three or four, go again. Most people need two or three rounds.
Even though I have this craving, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though I feel this stress, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though I've been hard on myself, I choose kindness now.
Close your eyes and picture the food you're craving. Make the image big, bright, close, notice how it pulls you.
Now imagine grabbing that image with your hand
push it far away until it's a tiny grey dot.
In its place, snap in a big bright image of you, confident, lighter, glowing, proud. Make it vivid: what are you wearing? How are you standing?
Say the word 'swish' in your head as the new image replaces the old one. Feel the shift.
Repeat 5 times, faster each time: craving image up, then swish, then confident you. By round five the craving image struggles to even form.
Open your eyes. Notice the craving now, most people find it's dropped from a shout to a whisper.
Remember a moment you felt completely calm and in control, a beach, a walk, a hug. Step into that memory: see what you saw, hear what you heard.
As the calm feeling builds, press your thumb and middle finger together firmly. Hold while the feeling peaks
Break state, look around, count 3 red things.
Repeat 3 more times with the same memory (or a new calm one). Same fingers, same pressure. You're wiring a physical 'calm button'.
Test it: press thumb and finger together
notice calm arriving. Use it before meals, in the biscuit aisle, or when stress says 'snack'.
Close your eyes. Imagine it's 6 months from now, and everything went well, you stayed consistent, kindly, imperfectly.
See Future You across the room. Notice her posture, her clothes, the ease in how she moves.
Walk over. Ask her: 'What was the one thing that mattered most?' Listen to what she says.
Ask: 'What should I stop worrying about?' Listen again.
Now step into her body. Feel what it's like, lighter, stronger, calm around food. Memorise this feeling.
Open your eyes and write down her two answers in your check-in this week. She's not imaginary, she's you, on schedule.
Old beliefs, like I can't do it, were learned. So they can be unlearned.
Which thought sounds like you? Pick the one that feels most true right now, or write your own.
Where do you think it came from?
A belief is just a thought you've thought many times. It was learned, not born with you, which means it can change.
One. When has this not been true, even once?
Two. What would you say to your best friend if she said this?
Three. What has believing this cost you?
Make it something you can believe today. A step forward, rather than a giant leap.
Edit the words so they feel like yours.
Every morning, it joins your mirror ritual. Say it out loud, looking into your eyes.
Every day, add one piece of proof. Small proof counts
a glass of water, a walk, a kind word to yourself.
When the old thought comes back, notice it, say that's an old thought, and repeat your new belief.
